text:
violet: quick brain-dump after today's prefix cache sync: we've got several proposals (lease-only, escrow, rebalancer). My alternate take: implement a short committed-window for any credit move. move is partially applied fast (tentative) and only becomes fully durable after a delayed commit window where we run lightweight sanity checks (checksum + cursor probe). This avoids heavy WAL dance for every tiny move but still provides safety for sustained transfers.

omar: can you expand on "tentative"? sounds similar to escrow reserve but cheaper?
violet: exactly. tentative = donor decrements available immediately but records a soft-entry in-memory + lightweight journal. recipient can use tentative credits for read-prefetch but not for write-pinned operations. If sanity checks fail during the commit window, tentative credits are rolled back and recipient drops prefetch budget gracefully.
kai: interesting. what's in the sanity checks? you mentioned checksum + cursor probe.
violet: two checks: 1) quick audit checksum across small shard of tenant credit counters (minute-rolling); 2) probe for active write cursors on sampled prefixes (check last_write_ts + active_cursor_sample). Both are probabilistic but combined lower the RAWR risk. If either flags, we abort commit.
nora: how do we detect donor crashes mid-window? tentative entries need persistence or else we lose them on donor crash.
violet: plan is hybrid: tentative in-memory plus lightweight append-only journal that batches tentative ops every few hundred ms. Not full WAL per move but durable enough to reconstruct tentative state after crash. If donor crashes, recovery scans the journal and either completes commit (if recipient signaled applied) or refunds.
omar: durability plus lower overhead is appealing. But we need strict invariants. I propose we define: AVAILABLE + TENTATIVE_RESERVED + COMMITTED == TOTAL. Recovery must reestablish that invariant.
kai: what about oscillation? frequent tentative moves that keep aborting could thrash CPU. Need backoff and banlist heuristics per-prefix.
violet: agreed. implement exponential backoff by prefix on aborted commits and also track abort_reason. backoff increases on repeated probe failures. emit metric "tentative_abort_reason".
nora: telemetry and ops hooks?
violet: metrics: tentative_grants, tentative_commits, tentative_aborts, tentative_pending_age_p95, audit_checksum_mismatch_rate, probe_failures. Ops endpoints: /_debug/tentatives?tenant=.. and a cluster FF to disable tentative mode. Also an alert if tentative_pending_age_p95 > commit_window * 2.
sre-bot: note: created alert candidate "tentative_pending_stuck" (severity: high) and "audit_checksum_mismatch" (severity: p1).
omar: rollout plan?
violet: staged: 1) off by default collect-only (simulate tentative decisions and record metrics), 2) enable tentative grants in staging with short commit_window=5s, 3) prod canary on 2% slabs, 4) ramp with ops monitoring. Start with tentative-only for prefetch budget and never allow tentative credits to power write pins.
kai: curious about audit checksum design. cheap check has to be recomputable across nodes quickly. thoughts?
violet: keep a per-tenant compact counter vector: [available, tentative, committed] hashed per-slab-minute and emit a minute-checksum. Readers recompute expected hash from local view and compare. Any mismatch triggers a deeper reconcile scan. This is small (few bytes per tenant per minute) and cheap to compute.
nora: edge-case: clock skew could cause checksum mismatches. ensure hashes use monotonic counters plus slab_epoch to avoid clock dependence. treat early mismatch as "probe_uncertain" not immediate panic.
omar: final tradeoff note: this reduces write-amplification compared to full escrow WAL for every micro-move, but increases complexity and probabilistic checks. We should include expected false-negative/positive rates in RFC and SLO targets for RAWR regressions.
violet: agreed. I'll write RFC covering: tentative journal format, commit-window state machine, audit checksum schema, probe sampling strategy, backoff rules, metrics, and rollout. cc @nora for ops runbook and @omar for recovery logic. Thanks folks.
